title: Symbolic Temporal Supervision of LLM Agents Using Contracts
summary: It replaces stochastic post-hoc LLM judges and per-call rule-based blockers with a single deterministic artifact: assume-guarantee contracts in finite-trace LTL, compiled to DFAs that gate tool calls online and evaluate recorded traces offline. The cost is engineering effort, not compute: someone must formalize checkable predicates over tool calls and author and maintain a correct contract library per task domain, plus DFA compilation overhead. It can fail when contracts are incomplete, wrongly specified, or the predicate set cannot observe the relevant state, in which case harmful actions pass deterministically or benign ones are blocked, and coverage does not transfer across domains without rewriting contracts.
rationale: The runtime is model-independent and cheap enough for constrained infrastructure, but the value depends entirely on the quality of manually authored contracts, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot rather than unconditional adoption. On constrained infrastructure this replaces expensive per-call LLM judging with a deterministic artifact whose main cost is upfront contract engineering, so a scoped pilot on one tool domain is the appropriate step. claims.statement: It replaces stochastic post-hoc LLM judges and per-call rule-based blockers with a single deterministic artifact: assume-guarantee contracts in finite-trace LTL, compiled to DFAs that gate tool calls online and evaluate recorded traces offline. The cost is engineering effort, not compute: someone must formalize checkable predicates over tool calls and author and maintain a correct contract library per task domain, plus DFA compilation overhead. It can fail when contracts are incomplete, wrongly specified, or the predicate set cannot observe the relevant state, in which case harmful actions pass deterministically or benign ones are blocked, and coverage does not transfer across domains without rewriting contracts.

Matches state-of-the-art LLM-judge and rule-based guardrail baselines across four benchmarks while producing deterministic, reproducible verdicts and, in online gating mode, orders-of-magnitude lower per-call latency than stochastic LLM judges.
